summary: First testing pass for Sorry Kitty (FastAPI + Supabase proxy + iframe-loaded vanilla HTML/CSS/JS frontend). Backend: 25/25 pytest tests passing — covers auth (signup/login/session/logout, duplicate email, short pw, missing fields, invalid token), cards CRUD (create/get/list/update/delete with owner-id authorization), chats (POST + GET ordered), notifications (POST/GET/PATCH read flag). Frontend: end-to-end happy path verified — signup → dashboard greeting (Hello, <name>!) → Create tab → fill recipient + message → Save 💾 → redirect to Cards list showing new card with character emoji, recipient, and Copy Link button → public share link (#card=<id>) renders the animated kitty viewer without requiring auth.

minor.issue: Error paths return HTTP 200 with {error:'...'} instead of 4xx. Works for the current frontend but is non-standard REST and may confuse other consumers / monitoring.
Returns raw array, while other endpoints return {success, ...}. Inconsistent envelope across the API.
Requires owner_id query param; missing param → FastAPI 422. No public/admin listing — acceptable but worth documenting.
If body has no 'user_id' the authorization check is skipped — any client could update any card. Should require user_id and reject when missing.

issues: Long single-column form scrolls below the fixed Save bar; the Save button at the top is fine but a user filling the form on a small viewport may not realize they can save without scrolling back up. Minor UX.

action_items: Consider returning proper HTTP status codes (400/401/404/409) for error paths instead of 200+error string.
Tighten PATCH /api/cards/{id} authorization: require user_id and reject when absent (currently skipped).
Normalize response envelope (GET /api/notifications returns bare list while others return {success,...}).
No retest needed for current scope — all listed acceptance criteria pass.
critical_code_review_comments: Password hashing uses base64 (`_hash_pw`) — this is encoding, not hashing. Acceptable only because the task explicitly says 'base64 hash' to match existing scheme, but it should be flagged as insecure for production. Recommend bcrypt/argon2 with per-user salt.

Supabase service_role key is committed in /app/backend/.env (and also redundantly in /app/frontend/.env as SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, which is also bundled in the vite client env). Even though the frontend code doesn't appear to use it directly, exposing service_role to Vite is risky — remove it from frontend/.env.
PATCH /api/cards lets you bypass ownership check by simply omitting user_id (see /app/backend/server.py L258-264).
No rate limiting / brute-force protection on /api/auth/login.
sessions never cleaned up — expired sessions accumulate; consider periodic cleanup.
server.py is a single 370-line module — fine for now but consider splitting auth/cards/chats/notifications into routers once it grows.

success_rate.frontend: 100% on tested flows (signup, login, create card, cards list, public share viewer)

test_credentials: Demo: qa.user@example.com / password123 — verified working. Sign-up is open; tests also create ephemeral test_<uuid>@example.com accounts.
seed_data_creation: Tests create transient TEST_ users/cards/notifications via API. Created cards are cleaned up via DELETE in the same test class. Notifications and ephemeral users are left in Supabase (no cleanup endpoint exposed).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend test file is /app/backend/tests/test_sorry_kitty.py — run with `pytest backend/tests/test_sorry_kitty.py -v --junitxml=/app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_results.xml`. Demo creds qa.user@example.com / password123 exist in Supabase. Frontend is iframe-based: main page at / loads /sorry-kitty.html in an iframe; tests must enter the iframe via `await iframe_el.content_frame()`. Public share viewer URL: /sorry-kitty.html#card=<id>. Note `c-recipient` etc. are real DOM ids but live inside a scroll panel — use scrollIntoView + JS .value + dispatchEvent('input') if Playwright fill() reports 'not visible'.
rca of the issue: n/a — no functional bugs blocking acceptance. Only minor design / security recommendations noted above.
